style.vernacular: Hot, humid Caribbean port city under the Blue Mountains. Downtown keeps 18th and 19th century Jamaican Georgian brick and stone buildings with timber fretwork, jalousie shutters and long galvanised-zinc hip roofs, plus low reinforced-concrete buildings of three storeys or fewer that replaced the stock lost in the 1907 earthquake (60 ft height limit). Uptown is concrete-block and rendered houses and offices painted in pale cream, yellow, pink and green with louvre windows, burglar-bar grilles, flat roofs and zinc roofs; towers appear only in New Kingston. Royal palm, mango, ackee, almond and samaan trees.
style.ornament: Jamaican Georgian timber fretwork and gingerbread trim on verandahs and gables; jalousie (louvre) shutters; white-painted quoins and cornices on brick; arcaded ground floors in downtown; burglar-bar grilles; bright painted murals and Rasta red-gold-green accents.

sources.what: 1692 earthquake and grid plan, brick city, post-1907 earthquake 60 ft height limit and 3-storey reinforced concrete, waterfront redevelopment
Jamaican Georgian: Flemish bond brick, limestone quoins, timber fretwork, dormers
Jamaica Georgian station: brick on stone base, sash windows, long zinc hip roof, timber posts on cast-iron brackets
